subtitle: A Taste of Yunnan

object_reference.name: A Chilli Pepper
object_reference.note: The narrator says they bring spices and seasonings, including chilli, from Yunnan and occasionally add them to food in Macau to retain hometown flavours. The pepper is a representative symbol, not a photograph of a documented family possession or an identified cultivar.

editorial_notes: This is the Yunnan-dialect aunt in interview 5, a different person from the Mandarin-speaking aunt in interview 2, as confirmed by the user. The supplied DOCX has no summary for this narrator.

The narrator describes growing up in Chuxiong until eighteen, five years of university life in Chengdu, postgraduate studies in Macau, several years of work in Kunming and a return to Macau. No exact migration year, institution, profession or order of degree completion versus the Kunming period is inferred.
Almost twenty years in Macau and the description of local climate and holiday patterns are retained as personal recollections, not independently verified chronology or statistics.
The closing example of mishearing Cantonese numbers remains unclear in the ASR source. The reading edition preserves the general recollection without inventing a phonetic explanation.
The chilli represents spices and seasonings brought from Yunnan at 14:15.250–14:43.700. No particular cultivar, family-owned specimen or exact preparation is documented.
The opening records agreement to be interviewed; it does not establish separate permission for online publication. Source and translation review statuses remain unchanged.

English quotations are translated and edited for clarity from the cited narrator passages. Window timestamps are not verified word-level quotation boundaries. All translations and edited passages remain drafts pending family review.
